diagnostic_evidence.quote: A standard fact (again, see \cite{kechris2012classical,srivastava1998course}) is that if Borel sets are coded in a standard way, then for a \textit{fixed} finite Borel measure $\omega$ on $\X$, the map \[ c\ \mapsto\ \omega(E(c,r)) \] is Borel as a function of the code $c$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof assumes a Polish space parameterizing all Borel functions with a Borel evaluation map. This is false: there is no standard Borel parameterization of all Borel functions with Borel evaluation; the usual Borel codes form a non-Borel, Π^1_1-complete set. Hence the constructed set B need not be Borel, and its projection need not be analytic.

failure_location.quote: Concretely, since $\X$ is Polish, there exists a Polish space of \textit{codes} $\mathsf{Code}(\X,\C)$ and a \textit{Borel evaluation map} \[ \mathrm{ev}:\mathsf{Code}(\X,\C)\times \X\to \C,\qquad (c,x)\mapsto \varphi_c(x), \] such that every Borel function $\varphi:\X\to\C$ is represented by some code $c$ with $\varphi=\varphi_c$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coding argument with a correct analyticity proof, e.g. using weak-* compactness of the L∞ unit ball, or weaken the route to use only the Borel reduction from IF_ω to A_{z0} for non-Borelness.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that A_{z0} is analytic and hence Σ^1_1-complete is unsupported. The proof of thm:route-IF-to-Az0(b) and the completeness route in thm:SCI_A_infty are invalid as written.
issues.title: Invalid coding of Borel functions in analyticity proof
issues.why_classification: The main non-Borelness and SCI_A=∞ conclusion can still be recovered from the Borel reduction alone, but the stated analytic-completeness claim needs a new nontrivial descriptive-set argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Now define $B\subset C(\X,\X)\times P$ as the set of pairs

issues.failure_explanation: B is a subset of C(X,X)×P and the conditions do not include F#ω<<ω. In the (⊆) direction the proof concludes F∈A_{z0}, but A_{z0} is defined inside Ω_X^∞, so F must be nonsingular. Without this condition K_F need not be well-defined on L∞, and the projection of B can include non-inputs.

failure_location.quote: Finally, we check that the projection of $B$ onto the first coordinate is exactly $A_{z_0}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the condition F∈Ω_X^∞ (equivalently F#ω<<ω) to the definition of B, and verify that this condition is Borel (or handle it in the analyticity argument).
issues.overall_effect: The proof that A_{z0} is analytic is incomplete; the set B may project outside the intended input class.
issues.title: Nonsingularity not enforced in analyticity construction
issues.why_classification: The missing condition is a local degenerate/input-class restriction; adding it does not change the main argument once nonsingularity is known to be Borel.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: be a measurable partition such that $0<\omega(\mathcal X_j)<\infty$ for all $j$.

issues.failure_explanation: The singleton {x_∞} has ω-measure zero in the Bernoulli product measure, but lem:Linfty-block-sap assumes every block has positive measure. Thus the lemma is invoked outside its hypotheses. The conclusion is still true after omitting the zero-measure block, but the proof as written has a gap.

failure_location.quote:

\[

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either omit the zero-measure block {x_∞} from the partition or extend lem:Linfty-block-sap to allow zero-measure blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The spectral decomposition step in lem:sap-FS-formula is not justified as stated, affecting the Silver-tree spectral equivalence and the L∞ type-G lower bound proof.
issues.title: Block decomposition applied to zero-measure singleton
issues.why_classification: A routine degenerate-case repair: zero-measure blocks do not contribute to L∞ and can be dropped without changing any substantive conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The odometer od_{m,u} is defined only for u∈{0,1,*}^m, but u_m(S) can be ⊥ (e.g. for S=∅). Thus F_S in def:Psi-Lip is undefined for such S. This contradicts the claim that Ψ is a total map on Tree_2 used in lem:FS_regular and cor:SCI_G_infty_alpha.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define od_{m,u} for u=⊥ (e.g. as the identity) and verify that the spectral equivalence and 1-Lipschitz property still hold.
issues.overall_effect: The 1-Lipschitz reduction is not well-defined for all trees, so the extension of the L∞ lower bound to the α-classes is unsupported as written.
issues.title: 1-Lipschitz map undefined when star-priority witness is ⊥
issues.why_classification: The missing case is a local degenerate case; setting od_{m,⊥}=id is a short fix that preserves the intended spectral equivalence.
